name: Thermite Cavity Disbursement Shell TCDS-3
description:
The TCDS-3 operates by firing a magnetically-stabilized shell casing packed with a proprietary nano-particulate thermite compound developed under contract with ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS. On impact or timed detonation, the outer casing fractures along pre-scored seams, releasing the thermite payload as a cascading aerosol that ignites upon contact with atmospheric oxygen. The burn sequence is not instantaneous — it sustains for four to seven seconds at temperatures exceeding 2,800°C, flowing into gaps, joints, and ventilation channels like liquid fire.

What distinguishes the TCDS-3 from conventional incendiary ordnance is its cavity-seeking behavior. The nano-particulate suspension is electrostatically charged prior to launch, causing particles to be attracted toward metallic surfaces and enclosed spaces — door seams, vehicle chassis, armored suits, server housings. Operators describe the effect as 'painting the inside of a wall.' The weapon is particularly devastating against hardened structures because it burns through reinforcement rather than blasting around it.

On the streets of GLMZ, the TCDS-3 is called 'Smelter' for obvious reasons. It is a weapon that leaves no survivors in a sealed space and no usable evidence in a burned-out vehicle. Corporate demolition crews use modified variants for precision structural teardown, but the weapon's proliferation into black market channels has made it a favored tool of arsonists-for-hire and syndicate enforcers settling property disputes permanently.
specifications:
shell diameter: 40mm
burn temperature: 2,800°C sustained
burn duration: 4–7 seconds
effective radius: 3.5m open / 8m enclosed
particle charge: -40 µC/g electrostatic
delivery system: Grenade launcher compatible, single-shot breach
weight: 0.9 kg per shell
safety window: 1.2 seconds post-launch arming delay
tactical_use: Used primarily for breaching hardened interiors — safe rooms, armored vehicles, reinforced server vaults. Operators fire through pre-drilled access points or ventilation grilles to maximize cavity exposure. Military sappers use it for structural column destruction. Syndicate operatives favor it for evidence elimination after wetwork in corporate offices. Not recommended in confined spaces without full thermal shielding — backwash kills operators who miscalculate room geometry.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's industrial lower districts, 'getting Smeltered' is slang for any situation where someone is dissolved from the inside out — financially, professionally, or literally. The weapon carries a grim prestige among demolition contractors and a reputation for cruelty among street-level enforcers. Possessing a TCDS-3 shell outside a licensed demolition context marks someone as either very well-connected or very dangerous, often both.
known_users: Insurgent cells targeting armored corporate convoys
Rogue ARCTURUS field testers operating off-books
story_hooks: A licensed demolition crew reports three shells missing from inventory — the shells turn up at the scene of a corporate board member's incinerated penthouse.
A black market arms dealer offers the party TCDS-3 shells at half price, no questions — the shells are stamped with ARCTURUS lot numbers that shouldn't exist for another six months.
Someone used a Smelter shell on a data vault the party was hired to crack. Everything inside is slag. The client insists the data was backed up. It wasn't.
An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the civilian demolition variant has a hidden firmware flag that can be remotely triggered — every licensed shell in the city is a sleeper weapon.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stubby, cylindrical grenade with an aggressive industrial aesthetic. The shell tapers slightly toward a blunt nose cone, giving it a purposeful, almost organic appearance despite its synthetic origin. The casing is segmented by visible pre-scored fracture lines running circumferentially, like stress points waiting to bloom open. The overall impression is one of contained violence — compact, dense, unapologetically lethal.
physical_description.dimensions: 40mm diameter shell body, 85mm total length including nose cone. Compact enough to nest in a standard grenade launcher magazine.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-weighted. The 0.9 kg payload feels concentrated, suggesting density rather than bulk. Sits heavy in the palm with an unmistakable sense of thermal mass waiting to be unleashed.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel outer casing with electrostatically-treated nano-particulate thermite compound suspension in the core chamber. Internal baffles of composite ceramic to withstand pre-ignition pressures.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with darker charcoal striping along the pre-scored fracture seams. The nose cone is slightly more polished to reduce drag, catching light differently than the body. Signs of oxidation or minor scarring typical of field ordnance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial gray and charcoal with rust-red accents appearing along the seam lines where the casing material has weathered. Minimal branding — functional, not decorative.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth and slightly cool to touch, with subtle grip dimpling near the base for secure launching. The nose cone is marginally rougher, possibly for detonator contact.
distinctive_features: Circumferential pre-scored fracture seams visible as dark stress grooves
Blunt, slightly flattened nose cone designed for impact detonation
Faint electrostatic discharge scoring on the metal surface — hairline traces of the charging process
Manufacturer serial etching near the base, barely legible without magnification
Subtle color gradient from gray body to darker charcoal at the seams, suggesting thermal stress distribution
Slight asymmetry to the nose cone — designed to tumble and orient for optimal cavity penetration
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Blackwood Commercial Group stamp on the lower third of the casing — a circular BCG logo with ARCTURUS DEFENSE sublicense notation. Serial number and hazard class etched in micro-script, visible only at close range under magnification. No bright warnings — this is black market ordnance, discretion built in.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but serviceable. Minor scuffing on the casing from magazine friction, possible discoloration from thermal stress during storage. Nose cone may show microscopic impact scarring. Often found in military-grade storage containers or syndicate armory cloth, suggesting careful handling despite its devastating purpose.
